subject: Order Form indemnity: escalation & evidence onboarding playbook
messages:
From: Rachel Alvarez <rachel@catalystai.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com
Date: 2026-06-07T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Order Form indemnity: escalation & evidence onboarding playbook

Hi Jonas,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Attached are the redlines Catalyst AI's counsel ran against the MSA + Order Form — we flagged indemnity (third-party IP claims) and evidence/notice timelines as the two items that will materially affect procurement timing. Quick summary of our position:

- For third-party IP claims, Catalyst asks to retain defense control for claims that arise solely from our data/instructions, but allows Redwood to step in if we decline.
- We propose a 30-calendar-day notice window from when the customer becomes aware to provide an initial notice to you.
- We want to preserve insurance offset language (we expect Redwood to deduct our insurance recoveries from indemnity payments).
- Evidence preservation: we need a clear list of what Redwood will collect if a notice is triggered (KV cache, prompt history, model/version, logs).

Can your legal and ops teams confirm:
1) Whether Redwood can accept the proposed notice window and defense sequencing;
2) What evidence artifacts Redwood can reasonably commit to preserve and for how long;
3) Whether liability cap language on the Order Form needs to be adjusted if defense control is retained.

Timing: procurement is expecting a finalized Order Form by the end of next week (2026-06-14). If we can do a 30-minute sync with your legal + ops tomorrow, that would help keep the timeline.

Attached: CatalystAI_MSA_Redlines_20260607.pdf (redline + short memo).

Best,
Rachel Alvarez
Senior Counsel, Catalyst AI
rachel@catalystai.com

Rachel — thanks for the detailed redlines and summary. Looping in Kimberly (legal) and Ben (sales ops) to get us aligned.

Quick notes from my side:
- We generally try to avoid unilateral defense-control clauses that let the customer run the defense in a way that prevents Redwood from protecting our broader platform. That said, I want us to be pragmatic here and see where we can compromise.
- Evidence/artifact list is the sticking point for our SRE/ops workload — we need to be explicit about retention windows and what we can snapshot quickly versus what requires escalated forensics.

Proposed next steps:
1) Kimberly/Ben — can you review the attached redline and provide (a) legal positions we can't move on and (b) operationally feasible evidence commitments?
2) Let's do a 30-min sync tomorrow 09:30 PT if that works for Catalyst.
3) I'll draft a short mutual action plan post-sync that maps legal signoff -> ops readiness -> procurement signoff.

If there are low-friction alternatives (e.g., accept 30-day notice but require an explicit defense-handback right after 10 business days unless Catalyst demonstrates progress), flag them in your reply.

— Jonas
Jonas Weber
Director, Strategic Partnerships
Redwood Inference

From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com, Rachel Alvarez <rachel@catalystai.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2026-06-07T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Order Form indemnity: escalation & evidence onboarding playbook

Thanks for the context, Jonas and Rachel. I reviewed the Catalyst redlines and added inline comments (attached). High-level reactions below — this is legal's recommended compromise posture to get procurement over the line while protecting Redwood's platform and other customers.

1) Defense control sequencing
- We can accept a customer-run defense for a narrow subset of claims that are demonstrably limited to the customer's prompts/data. But Redwood must retain an immediate right to assume defense if customer conduct or parallel claims could expose platform-level risk. Suggested language: customer has initial control for 10 business days; Redwood may assume control thereafter for platform-protective measures.

2) Notice window
- We are willing to accept a 30-calendar-day notice window if Catalyst accepts a clear obligation to provide a good-faith update within 5 business days after notice and to cooperate with Redwood's reasonable discovery requests. Note: the 30-day window should not be a limitation on the promptness of preservation steps.

3) Evidence preservation commitments
- Operationally feasible artifacts Redwood can commit to preserve upon notice: request logs (last 90 days), model name/version, serving configuration, KV cache snapshot for the session ID(s) in question (when available), and token-level timestamps. We cannot commit to full training datasets or long-term prompt archives without a separate, scoped forensic agreement and cost-sharing.

4) Insurance offset & cap interplay
- We cannot accept language that automatically offsets Redwood's indemnity payments by the customer's insurance receipts without a carveout for defense costs. We propose: insurer recoveries reduce indemnity payments after deduction of documented defense costs.

5) Suggested operational SLA and playbook
- We should add a 3-tier evidence-escalation playbook: (A) basic notice (low lift, auto-archive artifacts), (B) forensics request (ops-run snapshot, up to 2 business days), (C) deep forensics (requires scoped SOW + cost estimate).

Action items (legal):
- I attached Redwood_legal_comments_20260607.docx with redline alternatives.
- Ben — can you comment on the feasibility of the evidence list above and provide estimated timelines and costs for tiers B and C?

Rachel — happy to take a short call to walk through language and close the Order Form. If we can finalize legal positions today, we can produce a revised Order Form for Catalyst procurement.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Order Form indemnity: escalation & evidence onboarding playbook

Adding ops perspective. Kimberly — the artifact/tier approach looks good and maps to what SRE can deliver without a deep-forensics SOW. Practical notes: 

- Tier A (auto-archive) — immediate upon notice: request metadata, session IDs, model/version, 14 days of request logs put into a short-term retention hold (we use an internal snapshot process). Low cost.
- Tier B (ops snapshot) — we can produce KV cache snapshots and extended logs within 48 hours but will need an ops ticket and a nominal charge when large volumes (>$1k dataset retrieval threshold).
- Tier C (deep forensics) — requires a scoped engagement with estimated turnaround of 5–10 business days and will be billed.

I attached a one-page mutual action plan that maps owners and SLAs: OrderForm_MutualActionPlan_v1.xlsx. Important operational asks for Catalyst: include at least one technical point-of-contact and retain prompt/session IDs in your app logs (we cannot reconstruct sessions without those IDs).

If Catalyst agrees to the contact + session-ID requirement we can accept the 30-day notice pathway with the defense-handback sequencing Kimberly proposed.

— Ben

Head of Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
